mesoscaleDiscussions.summary: The severe threat may spread southeastward into late evening

details.label: Summary
details.text: The severe threat may spread southeastward into late evening

details.label: Discussion
details.text: A small cluster of storms has recently become somewhat better organized south and southwest of Jamestown, ND, with a recent gust of 77 mph observed in McIntosh County. The 00Z ABR sounding depicted substantial CINH for surface-based parcels, though considerably weaker CINH and strong buoyancy for parcels rooted around 850 mb. This thermodynamic profile within a modest warm-advection regime may allow for persistence of the ongoing cluster into late evening as it moves southeastward, assuming the cold pool remains sufficiently strong. Severe gusts (potentially near/above 75 mph) will remain possible with this cluster as it moves into northeast SD, while isolated hail will also be possible with the strongest embedded cells. WW 624 has been expanded in order to address this threat

mesoscaleDiscussions.summary: The risk of large hail and damaging wind gusts continues spreading eastward across parts of eastern North Dakota -- within Severe Thunderstorm Watch 625

details.label: Summary
details.text: The risk of large hail and damaging wind gusts continues spreading eastward across parts of eastern North Dakota -- within Severe Thunderstorm Watch 625

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Following several storm splits and associated mergers, a small upscale-growing cluster has evolved along the surface front in south-central/southeast ND. Over the next couple hours, this cluster will continue southeastward and pose the greatest risk of damaging wind gusts -- given the well-established cold pool and strong surface-based buoyancy downstream. Additionally, left-movers evolving northeastward in north-central SD could interact with this cluster and result in additional upscale growth. However, the 00Z ABR sounding sampled robust low-level inhibition at the base of the EML, which may limit the severe risk with southeastward extent into parts of northeastern SD. Farther north, a separate convective cluster/left-mover is tracking northeastward across parts of northeastern ND. Around 45 kt of 0-6 km shear (per MVX VWP data) oriented perpendicular to the surface front and moderate surface-based buoyancy should help maintain this cluster for the next hour or two. Large hail and damaging winds will be the main concern with this activity
